transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. I guess I'm here because... well, I've been having a hard time with my eating. Usually on late work nights, I’ll order what I tell myself is just going to be dinner. But then it turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert, and then I'll even keep going and get extra snacks from my kitchen. It just ends up being way more food than I’d ever eat if someone were actually sitting across from me.
After these episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don't. I've never done that. I just... I just feel really awful and full afterwards, but I don't try to throw it up or anything.
When this happens, do you feel like you can't stop eating or control how much you're eating?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start, there's just... this point where I'm almost watching myself keep going. Like I'll be opening another package, and in my head, I'm thinking that I really should stop, but it feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands. I just can't seem to stop myself.
After these eating episodes, do you ever try to make up for them by fasting, exercising a lot, or using laxatives or diuretics?
No, I don't do any of that. I don't take anything or try to exercise it off... I just kind of sit with it.
During these episodes, do you eat what most people would consider an unusually large amount of food?

Yeah, definitely. Usually it happens on these late work nights. I’ll order what I tell myself is just dinner, but it turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert... and then I'll even grab extra snacks from my kitchen on top of that. It's way more food than I’d ever eat if someone were sitting across from me.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?
Yes, it does. I feel really guilty and ashamed afterward. It's very upsetting to me.
How often do these eating episodes happen?

Well, when I look back at my delivery receipts and my calendar, there's usually at least one night every week where this happens. Sometimes more. And, um, that pattern has been going on for several months now.
